newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pac in talks to buy China terminals.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pac in talks to buy China terminals.

text.p: COSCO Pacific Ltd said on Wednesday it is in negotiations with its parent on the potential acquisition of certain China port terminals from its parent.
COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd, a wholly-owned unit of China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO), has a 56.6 percent interest in COSCO Pacific as of September 1996.
COSCO Pacific said it had noted recent reports concerning the company's potential acquisition of some China port terminals from its parent.

"The company confirms that it is in negotiations with its parent company and if any agreement is reached in relation to the above, a further announcement will be made," COSCO Pacific said in a statement to the stock exchange.
"Shareholders and warrantholders should exercise caution when dealing in the shares and warrants of the company," COSCO Pacific said.

COSCO Hong Kong, which has interests in container terminals in at least six Chinese cities, has said it would possibly inject some of its Chinese terminals into COSCO Pacific, its listed arm in Hong Kong.

As at April last year, COSCO Hong Kong owned 17.5 percent of Shenzhen's Shekou container terminal and five percent of the Yantian terminal near Shenzhen, and controlled 10 percent of operations in Shanghai's three terminal complexes.
It also owned 50 percent of the Qingdao terminal and 50 percent of Beilungang, China's biggest deep water harbour located near Shanghai, and 51 percent of Zhangjiakou on the Yangtze river.
